record.context_brief: Existence of a generator for analytic semigroups
record.original_question: Let (T (t))t≥0 be a not necessary strongly continuous semigroup on a Banach space X and consider the following condition. (i) (0, ∞) ∋ t 7→ T (t) ∈ L(X) is analytic. (ii) t 7→ T (t) is analytic on a sector containing R+ (iii) kT (t)k ≤ Metω , dtd T (t) ∈ L(X) and k dtd T (t)k ≤ Mt etω for some constants ω, M. Under which assumption added to (i), (ii) or (iii) does there exist a sectorial operator A generating (T (t))t≥0 ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space and let $\mathcal{L}(X)$ denote the Banach algebra of bounded linear operators on $X$. Consider a family $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}\subset \mathcal{L}(X)$ which is a semigroup, i.e. $T(0)=I$ and $T(t+s)=T(t)T(s)$ for all $t,s\ge 0$, but which is not assumed to be strongly continuous at $0$. Consider the following possible regularity conditions:

(i) the map $(0,\infty)\ni t\mapsto T(t)\in \mathcal{L}(X)$ is analytic (in the operator-norm topology);

(ii) the map $t\mapsto T(t)$ extends to an analytic $\mathcal{L}(X)$-valued function on some open sector of the complex plane containing the positive real axis $\mathbb{R}_+$;

(iii) there exist constants $\omega\in\mathbb{R}$ and $M>0$ such that for all $t>0$,
$$\|T(t)\|\le M e^{t\omega},\qquad \tfrac{d}{dt}T(t)\in\mathcal{L}(X),\qquad \Big\|\tfrac{d}{dt}T(t)\Big\|\le \frac{M}{t}e^{t\omega}.$$

Recall that a closed densely defined operator $A$ on $X$ is called sectorial if its resolvent set contains a sector $\{\lambda\in\mathbb{C}:|\arg(\lambda-\omega_0)|<\tfrac{\pi}{2}+\theta\}$ for some $\omega_0\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\theta\in(0,\tfrac{\pi}{2})$, with appropriate resolvent estimates, and one says $A$ generates the analytic semigroup $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ when $T(t)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma e^{\lambda t}(\lambda-A)^{-1}\,d\lambda$ on a suitable contour $\Gamma$.

Problem: Determine minimal additional hypotheses, on top of (i), (ii), or (iii) respectively, which guarantee the existence of a sectorial operator $A$ on $X$ that generates the semigroup $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about characterizing when a not-necessarily strongly continuous analytic semigroup on a Banach space admits a sectorial generator. No published resolution was located, and the standard theory (Lunardi, Engel–Nagel) handles the strongly continuous case but not the general framework asked here.

status_evidence.title: Analytic semigroups and optimal regularity (Lunardi)
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference treating sectorial operators and analytic semigroups under strong continuity assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Classical theory addresses analytic semigroups with sectorial generators primarily under strong continuity, leaving the non-strongly-continuous case as posed here unsettled.
